name: Ohana Fiber Mill
old_description: We make quality fiber from local Hawaiian wool, keeping production close to home and connected to the land. Simple, natural, and made with care.
about:
Ohana Fiber Mill operates in Honokaa on the Big Island of Hawaii. The business was founded by Alisha and Chris, who turned a love for the island into a venture that transforms local wool into sustainable fiber. No founding year is publicly stated.

The mill provides custom fiber processing from raw wool to finished skeins and produces its own 100% Hawaiian-grown and processed yarn blends. Those blends use Merino and Romney wool sourced from Kahua Ranch and other small local fiber producers. The facility is described as a cozy, historic space that also houses a retail store selling handmade items.

The company works directly with local wool producers, makers, farmers, and artists, building a regional network around Hawaiian fiber. Customers include individuals seeking custom processing services and buyers of the mill's own yarn collections.

The founders frame the mill as a way to keep Hawaii's fiber story alive, emphasizing connection to the land, the animals, and the community. The space is also intended as a gathering place for creativity and learning.
